llm.summary: Markets enter Black Friday's shortened session with the AI complex staging a violent mean-reversion: after roughly $6trn of market cap was wiped out, roughly $3trn came back this week as Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO and chip names led a rebound — though NVDA itself is still down ~28% on the month and now sits on S&P negative watch. The macro backdrop has turned genuinely awkward: Q3 GDP was revised sharply higher to 4.3% while the Fed's preferred PCE gauge hit 3.8%, the hottest since 2023, pushing December rate-HIKE odds up and lifting the 10-year toward 4.85% and 30-year mortgages to 7.21%. That combination — hot growth, hot inflation, tightening policy — maps directly onto the regime read of Reflation 37% / Stagflation 31%, with Goldilocks collapsing. Flows corroborate the rotation: Consumer Staples, Health Care, Real Estate and Utilities are being bid, Technology flows are deteriorating hard (sector rotation score -83), and Value is beating Growth by 103 points. The second-order AI story is now political and physical, not financial: Blackwell racks surfacing in Shanghai, export curbs halting Nvidia server shipments into Southeast Asia, GPU sellers policing neocloud resales, and a congressional hearing ahead — supply-chain legitimacy, not demand, is the new bear case. Beneath the noise, the real tell is that AI usage is exploding while incremental spend stalls, SAP is cutting 10,000 jobs in an AI push, and power/grid names (Duke, National Grid, Constellation) keep raising guidance on demand that is already contracted. The model portfolio — insurance, managed care, pharma, distribution, logistics, housing products — is positioned almost exactly where capital is rotating, with the main vulnerability being rate-sensitive consumer and housing exposure (MAS, BBY, DAL) if the Fed actually hikes. Today is low-liquidity and headline-driven; the week ahead (payrolls, eurozone CPI, OPEC+, Salesforce) is where the real test is.

market_thesis.short_term: Choppy and reflexive. The AI rebound is a short-covering/dip-buying bounce into a half-day holiday tape with VIX down 26.6% in a week — thin liquidity exaggerates upside. But rising yields, hawkish Fed repricing and an S&P negative watch on Nvidia cap follow-through. Expect continued violent rotation rather than a clean index trend: defensives and value grind higher, mega-cap AI stays volatile with a downward bias into the payrolls print and the Nvidia hearing.
market_thesis.medium_term: Over the next few months the dominant trade is dispersion within AI and breadth outside it. Hot nominal growth (4.3% GDP) plus 3.8% PCE means the discount rate stops helping and earnings have to do the work; that favours cash-generative value — insurers, healthcare, staples, utilities, grid — over long-duration software and GPU beta. The AI capex cycle does not end, but it bifurcates: power, cooling, memory, networking and custom silicon hold up while merchant GPU margins face export-control, resale-policing and credit-spread pressure (rising debt insurance costs at Nvidia, Oracle, Meta). A December hike would be a 5-8% drawdown catalyst for the Nasdaq and a relief for the value book.
market_thesis.long_term: Structurally, electricity is the binding constraint on intelligence. The decade belongs to whoever owns generation, transmission, transformers, cooling, copper and uranium, plus the compute that sits on top. Simultaneously, the AI build-out is becoming a geopolitical allocation problem — export controls, chip smuggling, hyperscaler-versus-hyperscaler competition for Latin American copper and power — which means duplicated, nationally-fragmented capex and persistently higher real rates. Inflation that averages above target with an aggressive public-investment and tariff regime argues for hard assets, pricing-power compounders and short-duration cash flows over the multi-year horizon.

short_term: Consumers are not in recession but are trading down: Black Friday shoppers are explicitly hunting value in Chinese-sourced goods despite tariffs, which supports dollar stores, Walmart and Best Buy's price-matched electronics rather than full-price discretionary.

Spending is bifurcating sharply by wealth — the richest Americans are materially increasing holiday outlays while everyone else budgets, so the same aggregate 'spending is on track' headline hides two different economies.

Homebuyers are responding to incentives, not affordability: new-home sales hit a 2026 high only because builders bought down mortgages and ran Black Friday promotions at 7.21% headline rates — demand is rate-subsidy dependent.

Investors are rotating from story to cash flow: Treasury yields now exceed bitcoin futures basis yields, killing the crypto carry trade, while long-duration Treasury flows increase and value outperforms growth by 103 points.

Households are feeling electricity as a cost shock — rising search interest in bill assistance, payment and calculators — which converts 'AI power demand' from an abstract theme into political and regulatory pressure on utilities.

Corporate behaviour is shifting from hiring to substitution: SAP cutting 10,000 jobs in an AI push and oil-field roughnecks losing roles to automation mark the beginning of visible AI-driven labour displacement in white- and blue-collar roles alike.
long_term: Knowledge and productivity are being bought as subscriptions and agents rather than headcount; the spend-per-seat model breaks down as usage explodes while spending stalls, forcing vendors toward outcome pricing.

Energy security becomes a household-level need, not a utility-level one: the 'when the grid fails, solar does not wait for the state' impulse drives behind-the-meter solar, storage and fuel cells as a consumer status and security purchase.

Security — physical, financial and digital — is a growing share of wallet: defence attention is spiking around drone warfare, cybersecurity attention is elevated with data-breach queries rising, and insurance pricing power persists.

Health is shifting from episodic treatment to continuous measurement and metabolic management, favouring continuous monitoring devices, diagnostics and the managed-care intermediaries that arbitrage cost.

Housing demand is being deferred and redirected: advice to young Americans to rent and invest instead, plus 7%+ mortgages, pushes capital toward renovation, repair and multifamily rather than new ownership.
Status is migrating from owned goods toward experiences, travel and access, sustaining airline and experience pricing even as goods deflate.

what_changed_since_yesterday: No prior brief exists for comparison; this is the first entry, framed against the past week's data.
Regime has shifted decisively: Goldilocks probability collapsed (-10.2) while Reflation (+13.6) and Stagflation (+8.6) both rose — the market is no longer pricing a benign disinflation path.
The Fed narrative flipped from cuts to a possible December HIKE after GDP was revised to 4.3% and PCE printed 3.8%, the hottest since 2023.
Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO, triggering a roughly $3trn market-cap snap-back after a $6trn washout — but S&P placed Nvidia on negative watch and the rally fizzled intraday.

The AI bear case migrated from valuation to enforcement and credit: Blackwell racks surfacing in Shanghai, halted Nvidia server shipments to Southeast Asia, GPU sellers policing neocloud resales, and rising debt-insurance costs at Nvidia, Oracle and Meta.
VIX collapsed 26.6% in a week, so hedges are cheaper than they were — a reason to buy protection rather than chase the rebound.
Treasury yields snapped an eight-day rally and turned higher, while the crypto carry trade broke as Treasury yields overtook bitcoin futures basis yields with BTC near $58,400.
Sector rotation extremes widened: Technology at -83 versus Consumer Staples 97, Health Care 91, Real Estate 83 — the portfolio's defensive value tilt is now aligned with flows rather than contrarian.
